# Los Angeles Rental Housing Obligations and Exemptions (as of October 1, 2026)

Based on the provided document, here are the operative rental housing obligations and exemptions that can be identified:

## RENT STABILIZATION ORDINANCE (RSO) - RENT CAPS

**Coverage:**

citations.cited_text:
Generally, the RSO applies to rental properties that were first built on or before October 1, 1978, as well as replacement units under
LAMC Section 151.28
and if any of the following:
Apartment
Condominium (Rent amount is not regulated for tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995)
Townhome (Rent amount is not regulated for tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995)
Duplex
Two or more single-family dwelling units on the same parcel
Rooms in a hotel, motel, rooming house, or boarding house occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days
Residential unit(s) attached to a commercial building
Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU)
Junior Accessory Dwelling Unit (JADU)
Mobile homes
and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks are also covered under the RSO.

content.text: The RSO applies to rental properties that were first built on or before October 1, 1978, as well as replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28, including apartments, condominiums (with rent amount not regulated for tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995), townhomes (with rent amount not regulated for tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995), duplexes, two or more single-family dwelling units on the same parcel, rooms in hotels/motels/rooming houses/boarding houses occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs), Junior Accessory Dwelling Units (JADUs), and mobile homes and recreational vehicles in mobile home parks.
**Allowable Rent Increases:**

content.text: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage.
**Rent Increase Restrictions:**

citations.cited_text: Effective March 30, 2020, through January 31, 2024, rent increases are prohibited for rental units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).

content.text: Effective March 30, 2020, through January 31, 2024, rent increases are prohibited for rental units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).
**Utilities Surcharge Prohibition:**

citations.cited_text: Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.

content.text: Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.
**Dependent Add-On Prohibition:**

citations.cited_text: Effective February 2, 2026, an additonal 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted.

content.text: Effective February 2, 2026, an additional 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted.
**Additional Tenant Increase (Enacted):**

citations.cited_text: However, a 10% for an additional tenant is allowed (not a dependent) if moves into a rental unit: Landlords can increase the rent within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.

content.text: A 10% increase for an additional tenant is allowed (not a dependent) if the tenant moves into a rental unit; landlords can increase the rent within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.

Rent may be increased to the market rate if the tenant:

does not pay rent and is evicted;
violated the lease agreement and is evicted;
is evicted for failure to comply with a Tenant Habitability Plan; or

content.text: Rent may be increased to the market rate if the tenant voluntarily moves out, does not pay rent and is evicted, violated the lease agreement and is evicted, is evicted for failure to comply with a Tenant Habitability Plan, or is evicted per a City Attorney order.

content.text: Rehabilitation Program: Landlords can recover costs for work in a unit or common area to comply with an order issued by LAHD or other government entities (RAC Reg 250).

citations.cited_text:

content.text: Just and Reasonable Rent Increase: A landlord can apply for a rent increase when their net operating income adjusted for inflation is not sufficient to cover the property's operating expenses (RAC Reg 240).
**Luxury Exemption:**

citations.cited_text:
Luxury Exemption
: A landlord can apply for an exemption from the RSO if they can establish the monthly rent charged on or before May 31, 1978,*.

content.text: A landlord can apply for an exemption from the RSO if they can establish the monthly rent charged on or before May 31, 1978.
## SURCHARGES (PERMITTED)

citations.cited_text:
A $1.61 monthly surcharge may be collected by the landlord as the tenant’s portion of the
Registration

content.text: A $1.61 monthly surcharge may be collected by the landlord as the tenant's portion of the Registration fee; effective January 1, 2020, the surcharge is $38.75.

citations.cited_text: The landlord may pass through 50% of the fee to the tenant every month rather than once a year.

content.text: The landlord may pass through 50% of the fee to the tenant every month rather than once a year.

citations.cited_text: A 30-day notice must be given to the tenant to collect a rental surcharge of $1.61.

content.text: A 30-day notice must be given to the tenant to collect a rental surcharge of $1.61.

citations.cited_text: Effective January 1, 2022, a landlord may collect 1/12 of 50% of the annual Systematic Code Enforcement Fee from the tenant of the rental unit per month.

content.text: Effective January 1, 2022, a landlord may collect 1/12 of 50% of the annual Systematic Code Enforcement Fee from the tenant of the rental unit per month.

content.text: A $3.00 surcharge may be added to the rent for the installation and cost of a hard-wired smoke detector or a combination smoke/carbon monoxide detector.

## JUST CAUSE EVICTION

**Legal Reasons for Eviction:**

citations.cited_text:
Legal Reasons for Eviction
Tenant is at-fault
Failure to pay rent
Failure to fix or address a violation of the rental agreement
Creating a nuisance or causing damage to the rental unit
Using the rental unit for an illegal purpose
Failure to renew a similar rental agreement
Failure to provide the landlord with reasonable access to the rental unit
The person at the end of the lease term is a subtenant not approved by the landlord
Tenant is not at-fault
The owner or immediate family member will move into the rental unit
A resident manager will move into the rental unit
Demolition and permanent removal from the rental market
Government order
Conversion to affordable housing
Eviction Notices
All notices to terminate a tenancy for all rental units subject to
City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO
) must be filed with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) within
three (3) business days of service on the tenant
per Los Angeles Municipal Code 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5.

content.text: Tenant at-fault evictions include: failure to pay rent, failure to fix or address a violation of the rental agreement, creating a nuisance or causing damage to the rental unit, using the rental unit for an illegal purpose, failure to renew a similar rental agreement, failure to provide the landlord with reasonable access to the rental unit, and when the person at the end of the lease term is a subtenant not approved by the landlord. No-fault evictions include: the owner or immediate family member will move into the rental unit, a resident manager will move into the rental unit, demolition and permanent removal from the rental market, government order, and conversion to affordable housing.

## REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS

citations.cited_text:
Required Registration and Posted Notification of RSO Rental Units
All Properties with RSO rental units must post a notification.

A landlord must serve a tenant with an
annual registration statement (Certificate).

content.text: All Properties with RSO rental units must post a notification, and a landlord must serve a tenant with an annual registration statement (Certificate).

citations.cited_text:
Beginning August 20, 2025, landlords must post the
Notice of Right to Counsel
and provide it to the tenant at the start of the tenancy. The Notice must also be attached to a copy of any eviction notice or termination of a rental subsidy.

content.text: Beginning August 20, 2025, landlords must post the Notice of Right to Counsel and provide it to the tenant at the start of the tenancy. The Notice must also be attached to a copy of any eviction notice or termination of a rental subsidy.

citations.cited_text:

registered annually

content.text: All units rented or offered for rent must be registered annually with LAHD.

citations.cited_text:

content.text: New property owners have 45 days to register their rental property and if applicable, file Temporary exemptions.

content.text: Beginning in 2017, in addition to paying the annual registration fee, landlords must also complete the Rent Registry form.
